parts.text: From Source 1, identify the estimated number of motor vehicles in the world in 2020.

parts.text:
Which consequence of large numbers of motor vehicles in cities do you think is the most

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Explain why large numbers of motor vehicles in cities is an important global issue.

text: Study Sources 1 and 2.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
‘We can improve transport in our cities.’
What are the strengths and weaknesses of the argument supporting this claim?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
‘Many people would like to travel by electric bus and tram.’
How could you test this claim?
You should consider the types of information, sources of evidence and methods you might
use.

text: Study Source 3.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify one value judgement from Mio’s statement. Explain why it is a value judgement.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Ren argues that government action is the best way to solve transport problems in cities.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Identify one opinion from Ren’s statement.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Explain how well this opinion supports Ren’s argument.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Which argument is more convincing, Mio’s or Ren’s?
Your answer should consider both arguments and you should support your point of view with
their words.
You should also consider:
• the strength of their reasoning and evidence
• their use of language
• the different kinds of information used.

text: Study Source 4.
A government wants to improve transport in cities.
The following actions are being considered:
• Research successful transport improvement projects used in other countries.
• Provide money to cities to promote cycling and walking.
• Charge more money to drive and park in cities.
Which one of these actions would you recommend to the government, and why?
In your answer, you should:
• state your recommendation
• give reasons and evidence to support your choice
• use the material in the sources and/or any of your own ideas
• consider different arguments and perspectives.
